Discussed intermittent TLS/PSK handshake failures during high-conn bursts, routing fallback behavior, quantization kernel upgrade plan, and telemetry gaps. Agreed on canary config and a 12-hour soak to validate fixes; Redwood to deliver updated runbook and notes on KV-cache/quantization impacts.
topics: handshake failures, PSK and mutual TLS, VPC egress shaping, fallback routing, quantization/kernel upgrade, telemetry enrichment (packet captures + traces), next-step soak and runbook delivery
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lara Kim (PocketPilot NetOps), Devon Park (PocketPilot SRE), Sofia Alvarez (PocketPilot Security), Tom O'Reilly (PocketPilot Infra)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, quick checkin. i can see the agenda in the deck link - sending again in chat, redwood-runbook-v2.pdf
[00:22] Lara: thanks Maya, yeah we've seen a couple of blips overnight; most of them were during the burst tests around 03:00 our time, high connection churn.
[01:05] Devon: to add, p95 token latency spiked and we saw ~0.3% handshake fails that recovered after fallback but it still caused a few user-facing retries.
[01:30] Ethan: ok, suspected area is PSK handshake timeouts on the on-prem gateway, possibly aggravated by the quantized kernel's socket scheduling, we've got a patch queued.
[02:10] Tom: just to be clear, we are running the kernel build qk-1.2.3, and the runtime reported some buffer-full errors in the logs, sometimes the KV cache warmup stalled under load.
[03:02] Maya: great, so today we're trying to confirm root cause: is it network (MTU/egress QoS), PSK timing, or the quant kernel? and then pick a remediation path.
[03:35] Lara: we ruled out MTU mismatches last week, but egress shaping is still a candidate; our egress is NAT+EGRESS-GW-A, with per-connection limits that might be pruning early.
[04:50] Devon: i can share packet captures for the failed handshakes, they look like truncated ClientHello sometimes, unclear if retransmit was dropped.
[05:14] Sofia: on the security front, we need to ensure any PSK change doesn't violate our KMS policy; we prefer KMS-backed PSK rotation, not manual.
[05:45] Ethan: noted, Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations; i'll put together a short note on supported modes and the SAML+audit implications.
[06:20] Maya: thanks. about fallback routing - last night the traffic fell back to hosted variant which preserved session but bumped cost. can you remind me how often that fallback triggers?
[06:55] Tom: fallback threshold is currently 5% error within a 60s window, l7 probe-based. it might be firing too aggressively during warmup spikes.
[07:40] Lara: yeah and those warmups coincide with KV-cache misses, so you get a cascade: miss -> slow token -> handshake timeouts -> fallback.
[08:12] Ethan: hmm cascade noted; we have two levers: tune fallback window and pre-warm KV cache using prefix caching and a short synthetic warmup. both can be implemented quickly.
[09:05] Devon: if we do synthetic warmup, we need to ensure no customer data is used; use dummy prompts. and we need telemetry to confirm effectiveness.
[09:40] Maya: agreed, we'll propose a canary: reduced fallback sensitivity (8% over 90s), synthetic warmup of top 50 prefixes, and a PSK handshake timeout bump from 2.5s to 3.5s for the on-prem gateway.
[10:20] Sofia: the PSK timeout change might be acceptable but check compliance — can't have indefinite retries.
[11:05] Ethan: also pushing an updated kernel build (qk-1.2.4) which addresses socket scheduling under high-conn churn; it's non-breaking but needs a rolling restart.
[11:40] Tom: rolling restart window? we prefer a maintenance window but for canary maybe a single node.
[12:01] Maya: propose one node canary, 12-hour soak, monitor errors and p50/p95/p99; if we see >0.5% regression we roll back.
[12:35] Lara: ok that works. Devon, you good to run the soak?
[12:48] Devon: yes, will run on canary infra and collect PCAP + metrics.
[13:22] Maya: log collection — we need trace ids and token-level latency breakdowns. Ethan will attach a small sidecar to emit KV-cache hits/misses.
[14:00] Ethan: sidecar is ready; small binary that scrapes runtime metrics every 5s. i will send config.
[14:45] Tom: also a note, our egress buckets have TCP connection caps per source IP, might need NAT pool increase for canary.
[15:18] Lara: raising NAT pool is ops heavy but doable, what numbers do you need?
[15:40] Maya: start with doubling for the canary. we can revert after.
[16:05] Devon: quick Q: quantization changes — will updating to the new kernel re-quantize models or is it purely runtime?
[16:40] Ethan: it's runtime only; however quantized kernels can change performance characteristics — we saw ~3% token throughput decrease in worst-case synthetic tests, but median improved. need to watch quality regressions.
[17:22] Sofia: on quality regressions, we require alerting if any eval set drops >2% on rouge or task accuracy during canary.
[17:50] Maya: we can wire Redwood Optimize to run a small eval set every hour during the soak and push alerts.
[18:30] Devon: perfect. also can we get a clearer mapping of which model variant falls back to hosted? last night it went from rdx-1-small to rdx-hosted-stable.
[19:02] Ethan: yes, will add explicit mapping table to the runbook.
[19:30] Tom: another log: we saw a handful of TLS alert 40s, which map to decryption_failed in our stack, might be indicative of PSK mismatch.
[20:05] Lara: so maybe a race during PSK rotation? we do rotate monthly, but not during tests.
[20:40] Sofia: if rotation is suspected, we need proof. can the Redwood sidecar log PSK id and rotation timestamps?
[21:10] Ethan: yes we can log PSK ID (not secrets) and rotation events to audit logs; we'll include that in the canary output.
[21:50] Maya: excellent. timeline recap: Redwood will provide updated runbook + canary YAML, kernel artifact (qk-1.2.4), and sidecar config by 2027-03-14. PocketPilot runs 12h soak on 2027-03-16 with increased NAT pool. metrics and PCAPs back to Redwood; we'll reconvene after soak.
[22:30] Devon: on the soak we'll collect p50/p95/p99, handshake fail rate, KV-cache hit rate, and packet captures for 5 sample failures.
[23:10] Lara: i want to emphasize telemetry gaps — we need traces that correlate user request id -> runtime token spans. can that be added?
[23:45] Ethan: yes we can propagate request IDs through the runtime and sidecar will emit spans. it requires a minor SDK tweak but it's low-risk.
[24:20] Tom: any thoughts on cost? if fallback goes to hosted variant during soak, costs could spike. we should cap fallback volume.
[24:55] Maya: we'll set a budget threshold for the canary -- 3% of traffic or $X/day, whichever comes first, and an automatic stop if exceeded.
[25:30] Sofia: legal check — any data leaving on-prem must be scrubbed; use synthetic prompts or anonymize.
[26:00] Ethan: sidecar will mask PII before sending any sample payloads; we'll show the masking rules.
[26:40] Devon: small interruption, we had a similar issue earlier with another vendor where kernel upgrades caused transient CPU spikes and circuit-breaker tripped. any mitigations?
[27:10] Ethan: we recommend ramped traffic profile: 10/30/60min step increases rather than full traffic cutover. and enable circuit-breaker backoff with jitter.
[27:50] Lara: good. also let's define success criteria: handshake failure <=0.1% sustained, p95 < 300ms, no quality regressions >2% on eval set.
[28:30] Maya: agreed. we'll codify that in the runbook.
[29:05] Tom: question about rollback — if kernel upgrade causes regression, what's the rollback time?
[29:30] Ethan: we can rollback within ~10 minutes per node, full rollback for canary cluster within 30-45 minutes depending on orchestrator.
[30:05] Devon: please confirm if any DB migrations or config changes are backward-incompatible.
[30:35] Maya: none for this patch, it's runtime-only.
[31:00] Sofia: security ask: provide evidence that audit logs (PSK rotation, auth attempts) are write-once and exportable to our SIEM.
[31:35] Ethan: Redwood audit logs can be forwarded to S3/CloudWatch or shipped to SIEM via syslog; we'll provide the config snippets.
[32:10] Lara: thanks. also small UX note — when fallback happens, clients see a 5s delay and sometimes duplicate messages; can we make the client-facing error clearer?
[32:45] Maya: we can add an error code that indicates 'degraded-inference-fallback' so clients can surface friendlier messaging. we'll include that in the SDK patch.
[33:20] Devon: any blockers for the canary? NAT pool change and a maintenance window on 2027-03-16. ops will approve.
[33:55] Tom: ops can do it, we'll need runbook steps for NAT pool sizing.
[34:30] Maya: i'll include explicit CLI steps.
[35:05] Ethan: small note on KV-cache warmup heuristics — i recommend seeding top prefixes from daily traffic heatmap; this reduces cold-start misses by ~60% in our tests.
[35:45] Lara: can you produce the script to extract top prefixes?
[36:10] Ethan: yes, i'll drop a one-liner and a short script in the runbook.
[36:45] Devon: telemetry format? we prefer JSON over newline logs so parsing is easier.
[37:10] Ethan: sidecar emits JSON lines by default.
[37:45] Sofia: will Redwood share a checklist for compliance sign-off? we need that before any long-running pilot escalation.
[38:20] Maya: yes, compliance checklist plus KMS integration notes will be in the handover packet.
[38:55] Lara: okay recap from our side: run NAT pool increase, prepare canary hosts, collect PCAPs and trace ids, run soak.
[39:30] Maya: recap from Redwood: runbook + canary YAML + kernel artifact + sidecar config + mapping table + small SDK error-code patch. due 2027-03-14.
[40:05] Devon: quick technical aside — when we collected PCAPs previously, timestamps drifted a bit between nodes due to NTP skew; can we ensure synchronized clocks?
[40:35] Tom: we'll ensure NTP is synced; i'll add a step in the soak precheck.
[41:05] Ethan: also will add sequence numbers to sample captures to align events.
[41:40] Lara: one more ask: if fallback triggers, capture a stacktrace or runtime debug dump automatically for first 3 events.
[42:10] Ethan: can do; small policy: only first 3 to avoid disk exhaustion.
[42:40] Sofia: on data residency, confirm that any logs sent to Redwood-owned buckets remain in our agreed region.
[43:10] Maya: yes, we'll pin region in the config.
[43:45] Devon: are there any licensing or pricing impacts for canary runs?
[44:10] Maya: for the pilot we agreed a capped credit; overages will be discussed but we'll aim to keep within the pilot budget.
[44:45] Lara: cool. anything else?
[45:15] Tom: just one curiosity — competitor Anthropic had a handshake optimization recently, did you notice any similarities in their approach?
[45:40] Ethan: superficially yes, they extended PSK timeout and pre-warmed sockets; but our fallback/routing semantics differ.
[46:10] Maya: ok final next steps and owners — we've captured action items in chat.
[46:45] Sofia: schedule follow-up after soak, maybe 2027-03-17 16:00 UTC?
[47:10] Maya: that works for Redwood. we'll send calendar invite.
[47:45] Lara: thanks everyone, appreciate the focus.
[48:05] Devon: thanks, signing off.
[48:20] Ethan: thanks all, will follow up with sidecar config link.
[48:35] Maya: end meeting.
